sources.title: Zipf's law - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Zipf's law (/ zɪf /) is an empirical law stating that when a set of measured values is sorted in decreasing order, the value of the n -th entry is often approximately inversely proportional to n. sources.title: Zipf's Law: Definition, Formula & Caching Applications
sources.snippet: Zipf's Law states that the frequency of an item is inversely proportional to its rank. Learn how this power-law distribution models content popularity in proactive caching.

sources.title: Zipf's Law and the Limits of Caching | Guido Steinacker
sources.snippet: Breslau et al. demonstrated in 1999 that web traffic follows a Zipf distribution. The consequence: a tiny fraction of all possible queries accounts for the majority of traffic. An example: An online shop receives 500,000 different search queries per day. The top 5,000 (i.e. 1%) generate 400,000 of these.
